discriminating_terms: was suspended. Consequently, many employees worked from home
attributions.rationale: “was suspended. Consequently, many employees worked from home” explicitly presents the latter clause as the result of the former. A merely temporal ‘after that’ reading is not supported, because the connective marks the suspension as the reason for working from home; the listed causal-result sense is therefore unique.

In “the application was consequently rejected,” consequently links the missed deadline to the rejection as its outcome. A simple-sequence alternative would leave that causal link unexpressed, whereas this adverb directly marks it; only the causal-result sense fits.

discriminating_terms: and consequently faces frequent water shortages
attributions.rationale: “and consequently faces frequent water shortages” makes facing shortages the consequence of receiving little rainfall. Reading consequently as only a later-time marker would not account for the result relation encoded between the two predicates, so the causal-result sense is uniquely selected.

In “the company consequently reduced production,” the reduction is framed as the consequence of demand falling sharply. The plausible noncausal sequence reading is excluded because consequently itself establishes the demand-to-reduction relation; this uniquely realizes the causal-result sense.

discriminating_terms: The evidence was incomplete; consequently, the committee postponed its decision
attributions.rationale: “The evidence was incomplete; consequently, the committee postponed its decision” explicitly casts the postponement as the result of incomplete evidence. It cannot be reduced to a neutral chronological transition, since consequently supplies the causal inference; the causal-result sense is the sole listed attribution.
